data.gender_notes: Balfour is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from Old French 'de Balfour', meaning 'of the fortified place'. The name became popular in Scotland, where it was used by those who lived near a castle or fortification. The name Balfour carries the meaning “Of the fortified place” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Balfour usually hope their child will grow to embody of the fortified place and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of protection and strength.
data.etymology: Balfour belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Of the fortified place.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balfour total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.
